issues.issue: Tomat and Wayscriber native GTK popups do not expose an authoritative active-button lifetime
issues.evidence: Signed Waybar 0.15.0 source shows AModule maps the native GtkMenu from the input event and then unsets PRELIGHT; it has no popup-open CSS class or deactivation callback. Signed Custom/util command source exposes only the close-on-exec stdout pipe for the continuous reader and separate forked click children; no documented or stable FD5/FD6 lifecycle channel exists. Private native replay 92 measured Tomat's button at the same normal-color pixels before and while the popup was mapped. The fixture later stopped at an unrelated btop theme-view assertion (GUEST_RESULT=1).
issues.implemented_change: Kept native in-process menu ownership and canonical XML/action maps, removed the duplicate misleading Tomat :active selector, documented launcher and Apps drawer lifetime owners, and retained Wayscriber's daemon .active state separately from pointer press state. No timer, compositor observer, fabricated serial, persistent invisible anchor or second popup owner was added.
issues.regression: Native replay 92 mapped and grabbed the Tomat popup and measured the expected normal-color state; the fixture stopped only at the unrelated existing btop theme-view assertion. Static source/API checks confirm that no FD5/FD6 lifecycle signal exists in the supported package.
issues.runtime_acceptance: Accepted native-package behavior: Tomat and Wayscriber retain their timer/daemon classes while the Waybar-owned GTK popup is open. Mapping, focus, input, dismissal and fixed action dispatch remain covered by the native menu acceptance; no fabricated popup-active color is required without a supported lifecycle signal.
